newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine will hear about IMF tranche in December.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine will hear about IMF tranche in December.

text.p: Ukraine will have to wait until mid-December before it learns whether the International Monetary Fund (IMF) will approve the next tranche of its $867-million standby programme, the IMF's resident representative said on Monday.
"The board reviews every other (second) tranche," Alex Sundakov told Reuters. "The next board meeting should be in the second week of December."
An IMF mission completed a visit to Kiev on Friday to review the next monthly tranche payment, usually worth about $100 million each.
It also continued negotiations for a three-year Extended Fund Facility (EFF) worth approximately $2.5-3.0 billion to follow the standby programme.
Sundakov would not comment on whether the EFF had been approved.
But sources close to the talks said the government was expected to announce an agreement in principal this week.
Ukraine has also requested a $1.5 billion stabilisation fund for the hryvnia currency, introduced in September, as part of the EFF.

Fund missions have been visiting Ukraine almost monthly to review economic progress and approve monthly disbursements. The IMF suspended payments to Ukraine for a time earlier this year after it overshot spending targets. --Irene Marushko, Kiev Newsroom +380 44 229 2264
